chunks.subject: AP Chemistry
chunks.title: Q4 — Short Answer (4 points)
chunks.content: AP Chemistry Q4 (Short Answer), 4 points, one per part. Topic: formaldehyde (H2CO) and methanol (CH3OH). A [Pt1]: hybridization of the C in H2CO is sp2 (three electron domains). B [Pt2]: draw a hydrogen bond — a dashed line between the O of H2CO and the H of the O–H group of CH3OH. C(i) [Pt3]: propose a temperature (181 K–254 K) at which both substances are liquids (between each one's melting and boiling points). C(ii) [Pt4]: energy released on condensation = moles CH3OH × ΔHvap (8.59 g → ≈10.1 kJ removed). Common failure: assigning sp3 to the trigonal-planar carbon; drawing an H bond from a C–H (too small a dipole); misusing q=mcΔT at a phase change instead of moles×ΔHvap.

chunks.subject: AP Chemistry
chunks.title: Q4 exemplar — Sample 4A, 4/4
chunks.content: Q4 scored 4/4. sp2 hybridization for the carbon (A); a valid hydrogen bond from the O–H hydrogen of CH3OH to the O of H2CO (B); 215 K correctly recognized as between the melting and boiling points of both, so both liquid (C i); moles of CH3OH × ΔHvap giving the energy removed on condensation (C ii). Full-credit model.

chunks.subject: AP Chemistry
chunks.title: Q4 exemplar — Sample 4B, 2/4
chunks.content: Q4 scored 2/4. Earned B (valid hydrogen bond) and C(i) (185 K, both liquid). Lost A (called the carbon sp3, which would need four domains rather than three) and C(ii) (used q=mcΔT with the boiling point as ΔT and water's specific heat, but no temperature change occurs at a phase change). Shows the common phase-change energy error.

chunks.subject: AP Chemistry
chunks.title: Q4 exemplar — Sample 4C, 1/4
chunks.content: Q4 scored 1/4. Earned only A (sp2 for the H2CO carbon). Lost B (drew the H bond from a C–H, whose dipole is too small), C(i) (chose 120 K, below both melting points, so both are solids; also misused a degree symbol for kelvin), and C(ii) (divided rather than multiplied by ΔHvap). Illustrates a response that secures only the hybridization point.
